summary: All checklist items hold. expression.py adds only collapse_series (no edit to _resolve, _as_number or _loose_equal), and it is applied in exactly two places in evaluator.py: the calculated-field result (before rounding) and the criterion `observed`. standard_group() always returns kind table with rows {min:1,max:10,default:1} and rowLabel {format:'STD - {n}'}. Importing SEED_TEMPLATES shows no standard or standard_2 group left as a singleton; standard_2 in TPL-A4-0001 is a table; TPL-A4-0004 standard has no renderAsTable. The A2-0004/A2-0005/A11 tables keep their own row specs and are not modified. The sync tool never copies a module over a live row: module_check only compares, and the write path updates just definition, modified_by and modified_date from convert_definition(stored definition). It aborts unless the fingerprint is 57 rows / Active 48, Draft 4, Inactive 3, Superseded 2 with integrity ok. It takes and checks a backup first, writes in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction with an in-transaction verify and rollback, and verify hashes every identity column (including version and status), so those stay untouched. No .agents or lims.db* file appears in the diff (the worktree is clean and .gitignore covers lims.db and lims.db.bak-*). The multi-row aggregate test exists (parametrized over 19 converted module templates, mean/sd/count over 3 rows, including standard_2 in A4-0001), and the four flat-mirror assertions now read result.rows['standard'][0]['conc_ppm']. The formula-preservation evidence is the old-vs-new replay harness (empty, synthetic, 3-row padded and stored-worksheet variants, comparing calculated cells, criteria and reportable result) with 0 diffs on the 25 live rows. This verdict rests on the recorded FEAT evidence and a read of the diff; I did not re-run the suites. Non-blocking notes for later steps: (1) --apply has not been run, so the live DB is still unconverted until the db-loop step. (2) The frontend add/delete behaviour rests on existing generic table handling and is covered only by the planned npm build in plan item 7, which no FEAT records yet. (3) The backup is taken just before BEGIN IMMEDIATE while uvicorn is live, so a worksheet write in that gap would not be in the backup. The in-transaction check that each target definition is unchanged, plus the worksheets hash, limit the risk to the backup copy only.
